hints: Follow the two reactions in order, first NaBH4 reduces the carbonyl to an alcohol, then hot Al2O3 dehydrates that alcohol to an alkene.
Draw the alcohol made from butanone, which is butan-2-ol, and notice H atoms can be removed from two different neighbouring carbons.
Remember to count both positional isomers of the alkene and cis-trans pairs for any C=C with two different groups on each end.
walkthrough:
**Reduce the carbonyl to the alcohol**

NaBH4 is a reducing agent. It turns aldehydes into primary alcohols and ketones into secondary alcohols.

$$\text{RCHO} \rightarrow \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}, \quad \text{RCOR'} \rightarrow \text{RCH(OH)R'}$$

**Dehydrate the alcohol to the alkene**

Heating with $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ at high temperature removes $\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The OH leaves from one carbon and H leaves from an adjacent carbon to form $\text{C=C}$.

**Check each starting carbonyl**

Butanal gives butan-1-ol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$. Only one elimination position, so only but-1-ene, with no cis-trans isomerism. That is 1 isomer.

Propanone gives propan-2-ol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$. Only propene can form. That is 1 isomer.

**Compare the two symmetrical and unsymmetrical cases**

Pentan-3-one gives pentan-3-ol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Elimination to either side gives the same skeleton, pent-2-ene, which exists as cis and trans. That is 2 isomers.

Butanone gives butan-2-ol: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Elimination gives two skeletons, but-1-ene and but-2-ene. But-2-ene then shows cis-trans isomerism, giving 1 + 2 = 3 isomers in total, the most.

options.A: Butanal is reduced to butan-1-ol, a primary alcohol. Dehydration can only give but-1-ene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, which has no E/Z isomerism. So only 1 product.
options.B: Butanone is reduced to butan-2-ol. Dehydration gives positional isomers but-1-ene and but-2-ene. But-2-ene, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3$, exists as cis and trans forms, so total is but-1-ene + cis-but-2-ene + trans-but-2-ene = 3 isomers, the largest number.
options.C: Pentan-3-one is reduced to pentan-3-ol, which is symmetrical. Elimination from C2 or C4 gives the same skeleton, pent-2-ene. This gives only cis-pent-2-ene and trans-pent-2-ene, so 2 isomers, fewer than for butanone.
options.D: Propanone is reduced to propan-2-ol. Dehydration can only give propene, $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_3$, with no positional or stereoisomers. So only 1 product.
